checks.claim: Fixedpoint (through the adapter) computes Souffle's relations, as the SHA-256 of the sorted tuples, on every case in every runtime
the independent naive evaluator also equals Souffle on every case (a third semantics agrees)
derivation heights rebuilt from Fixedpoint's relations equal the heights of Souffle's explain trees on every derived tuple, and every rebuilt step is an instance of its rule
native Z3 and Pyodide in Node, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit give the same corpus digest
no program that Souffle rejects is accepted by the adapter, and every program both accept gives equal relations
Souffle's compiled mode gives the interpreter's relations on the cases tried
the comparison fails when the engines are given a deliberately wrong program

notes: The S7 fixtures of this record are the ones the curriculum defines today: the toy of LAB-7.1, the reference world W0 and its variants, seeded worlds with the section 1 parameters (some break WF1 to WF3 on purpose), the policy mutants of LAB-7.c3 and the Prove-it table, S7.L2's English variant, a role-permission policy of fourteen rules that differ only in constants, and Souffle's transitive-closure example with negation over the recursive relation. W4-T07 runs the same comparison on the authored fixtures.

Relations are compared as the SHA-256 of the sorted tuples (each tuple a line, columns tab-separated, a final newline), the form LAB-7.c1 names. The adapter is scripts/spikes/W0-S03/ss_datalog.py: a parser and checker for the Souffle subset S7 uses, a translation to Fixedpoint, and a reconstruction of derivations from the relations.

Heights follow Souffle's explain trees: a leaf (a fact, a negated atom or a comparison) has height 0 and a rule node has 1 + the largest child height. Souffle prints proof trees of minimal height; the adapter computes minimal heights from Fixedpoint's relations. The explain shell prints a constraint with symbol ordinals (21 != 18) instead of the symbols (explain-read-ref-w0.txt), so the run reads heights from its JSON form, with setdepth 100 so that deep trees print in full, and not from the text.
Z3's own derivation facility (datalog.generate_explanations) is not used: probes.json shows it answering wrongly or crashing on programs that the default setting answers correctly.

This is not a phone run and not the custom-subdomain origin: the browser runs are headless desktop engines in a container, served from one local origin with no COOP or COEP headers (W0-S01 and W0-S02 own those). Timings are from a machine with 20 CPUs of which the container was allotted 4; Firefox and WebKit round performance.now to whole milliseconds. A relation's contents do not depend on the device, its speed does.
The installed Souffle binary hash e8e4d8bff0b8377d2d42ae30886121a61061ec0c8bb948f1f5129e09aecfa9a1 comes from the same upstream package that RUN-souffle-version pins.
Paths are normalised: <repo>, <work> and <cache> stand for directories on the machine that ran this.
